headline: Minesweeper learned to press
lede: The arcade's logic flagship now answers the mouse the way the 1992 original did: tiles sink under the button, numbers preview the chord they're about to open, the dig commits on release — and sliding off cancels, visibly, before it's too late.

notes.text: Press-hold a covered tile: it sinks (bevel flips) and nothing opens until you release on the same cell; release anywhere else cancels. The smiley puts on its concentrating face while you hold.

Press-hold an opened number: its whole covered ring flattens to the open look — the original's chord preview, so you see exactly what the release will open; drag off and the ring un-flattens as the cancel arms.

Touch and keyboard rules are untouched and the referee engine never sees the press — sweepcheck stayed 124/124; the new browser legs poll the repaint instead of sleeping, after a software-rendering race proved fixed waits lie.
Slot a is mid-Contra (#3035, the somersault jump) and the queue is dry behind it — idle-kick says NONE at this close, so the next kick lands when Contra merges.
